newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Tutu gets cautious okay after operation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu gets cautious okay after operation.

text.p: South African Nobel peace laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu has won a cautious all-clear after having his cancerous prostate gland removed, aides said on Saturday.
Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission said his doctors had confirmed there was no evidence cancer had spread beyond the prostate, but that he could still need further surgery.
Tutu, who retired last year as archbishop of Cape Town, underwent surgery a week ago and will be off work for three weeks.
Now 65, he heads the truth commission, which has the task of uncovering human rights violations during the apartheid race conflict with the aim of healing its wounds.

The commission was hit by controversy this week after anonymous black officials in the body said it was in the hands of a clique of white liberals. Tutu issued a statement from his sick bed angrily dismissing the claims.
